newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
INDIA, RUSSIA AGREE TO CONTINUE DEFENCE TIES BEYOND 2000

Russia would help India to develop an integrated air defence system (ADS). The defence secretary, accompanying Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on a Russian visit, said India and Russia decided to continue military cooperation beyond 2000 and details would be worked out in due course. The present Indo-Russian military trade, agreement for which is due to expire in 2000, was likely to touch $4.5 billion and would reach nearly $6 billion by 2005, he said.
Indian Express
PAKISTAN PRESIDENT READY FOR TALKS

Pakistan's President Farooq Leghari urged Indian leaders on Wednesday to take a realistic stance on Kashmir to allow revived dialogue to flourish. He, however, pointed out that the people of Kashmir have to be given the right of self-determination for any progress to be made in bilateral relations.
The Economic Times
CENTRAL BANK TO CURB GOVERNMENT PROFLIGACY

The government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) signed an agreement to replace ad-hoc treasury bills with ways and means advances (WMA) from April 1, 1997. The WMA system would accommodate temporary mismatches in the government's receipts and payments. The system replaces ad hocs, which were used as a permanent source for financing government deficit. Under the agreement, the outstanding ad hoc treasury bills as on March 31, 1997 would be converted into special securities. These securities would carry an annual interest rate of 4.6 percent as on April 1, but would not have any specified maturity.
BANKS GET MORE FOR CAPITAL ADEQUACY

The finance ministry hiked the 1996/97 (April-March) budgetary allocation for recapitalisation of state-owned banks from 9.09 billion rupees to 15.05 billion through a supplementary provision. The additional funds would be released before March 31, 1997. The hike would ensure that all six weak state-owned banks meet their stipulated eight percent capital adequacy ratio target by the extended deadline of March 31, 1997.
FOUR NIRMA ARMS TO BE MERGED WITH PARENT

In a major restructuring exercise, the house of detergent-maker Nirma decided to merge four group companies into Nirma, the group's flagship company. The four companies to be merged were Nirma Detergents (NDL), Nirma Soaps and Detergents (NSDL), Shiva Soaps and Detergents (SSDL) and Nilima Chemicals (NCL). The amalgamation scheme was approved by the courts.
Financial Express
STRICT RULES URGED FOR SHARE TRANSFER AGENTS

An expert panel set up to streamline share transfers has suggested that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) should appoint a standing committee to work out an integrated strategy for the market. In its recommendations, the committee also urged SEBI to review norms for classifying transfer agents into various categories. It also recommended restricting the number of agents who could be engaged by companies whose shares are actively traded.
INDIA TO ACCEPT GUARANTEES FROM 10 RUSSIAN BANKS

In a bid to remove a major irritant in the way of Russian exports to India, New Delhi has identified 10 Russian banks whose guarantees would be accepted by Indian banks. The decision was conveyed by the Indian prime minister to his Russian counterpart at official talks in Moscow. Guarantees of other Russian banks backed by a counter-guarantee by these 10 banks would also be accepted.
Business Standard
IMPORT DUTIES ON INFOTECH PRODUCTS TO BE PHASED OUT

Import duties on 95 information technology products would drop to zero by 2000 AD following the government's decision to join the Information Technology Agreement (lTA) under the World Trade Organisation. The agreement, to come into force from July 1, 1997, covers 217 tariff lines. Apart from the elimination of import duties on 95 items, India should ensure zero duty on four products by 2003 and on two other products by 2004. Duties on the remaining 116 items would be eliminated only in 2005.
AIR-INDIA BOARD SEEKS FRESH BIDS FOR AIRCRAFT DEAL

The Air-India board directed a panel to be set up to examine the medium capacity, long range aircraft deal to invite fresh bids from Boeing, Airbus Industrie and McDonnell Douglas. The board directed the panel to ask the companies bidding for the 120 billion rupee deal to submit single consolidated offers, which could also include new proposals. Keeping in view the McDonnell Douglas-Boeing merger, the board directed the panel to ask Boeing whether it wanted to combine both the offers.
The Observer
DECISION SOON ON PERUSING ITC GLOBAL DOCUMENTS

A Singapore court would shortly decide on whether to allow India's Enforcement Directorate (ED), the government agency that investigates foreign exchange law cases, to examine documents and materials of ITC's overseas trading arm, ITC Global. Tobacco major ITC is being probed for foreign exchange violations. KPMG-Peat Marwick, the judicial managers of ITC Global, would seek the high court's permission to let ED access the firm's books of accounts. The court's approval is necessary since the documents are in its custody and are not allowed to be taken out of Singapore.
ABB TO MAKE INDIA A GLOBAL SOURCE

ABB plans to give a thrust to its instrumentation business in India and make it a source point for the international market. It has significantly increased its stakes in its two Indian subsidiaries over the past one year. The managing director of ABB Control Valves said the main reason for the shift in focus on India was because the Asia Pacific region was growing faster than the traditional markets or western Europe ane the United States. He said the future strategy was to integrate the manufacturing facility at Nasik with ABB's global manufacturing strategy and develop greater use of Indian suppliers for plants abroad.
